content: 1. Practice Setting: Please identify the type of healthcare setting in which you practice. 2. Number of Providers: Indicate the total number of healthcare providers, including yourself, who deliver family planning services in your practice or health center. 3. Provider Role: Specify your role as a healthcare provider. 4. Patient Volume: On average, how many female patients of reproductive age do you see per week? 5. Training in Contraceptive Methods: Have you been trained in the insertion and removal of the following contraceptive methods during routine care? These include copper intrauterine devices (Cu-IUDs) and levonorgestrel-releasing intrauterine devices (LNG-IUDs). Please answer yes or no for each method. 6. Postpartum Contraceptive Training: Have you been trained in the insertion and removal of Cu-IUDs and LNG-IUDs immediately postpartum? Please answer yes or no for each method. 7. Contraceptive Availability: For each contraceptive method, indicate whether it is directly available onsite, prescribed/recommended for offsite access, patients are referred offsite to other providers, or it is not available at all. Methods include LNG-IUDs, Cu-IUDs, implants, combined oral contraceptives (COCs), progestin-only pills (POPs), injectables (DMPA-IM, DMPA-SC, NET-EN), contraceptive patches, vaginal rings, diaphragms, male condoms, female condoms, emergency contraceptive pills, and Cu-IUDs as emergency contraception. 8. Provision of IUDs to Nulliparous Women: In the past month, how often have you or your clinical team provided IUDs (Cu-IUDs or LNG-IUDs) to nulliparous women? If not often or never, please indicate the reasons, such as lack of nulliparous patients, unavailability of IUDs, safety concerns, concerns about future fertility, difficulty with insertion, lack of training, patient preference for other methods, or practice protocols prohibiting it. You may also specify other reasons. 9. Exams and Tests Before Contraceptive Initiation: Before initiating specific contraceptive methods, indicate which exams or tests are required for a healthy patient. Specify if the method is not offered or available in your practice. 10. Quick Start for Combined Hormonal Contraceptives: In the past year, how often have you initiated combined hormonal contraceptives (COCs, patch, ring) on the same day as the patient’s visit, regardless of menstrual timing, if reasonably certain the patient is not pregnant? Please answer separately for adolescents and adults. If not often or never, indicate reasons such as safety concerns, liability concerns, lack of training, appropriateness for the patient population, or practice protocols. You may also specify other reasons. 11. Quick Start for Injectable Contraceptives: In the past year, how often have you initiated injectable contraceptives (DMPA or NET-EN) on the same day as the patient’s visit, regardless of menstrual timing, if reasonably certain the patient is not pregnant? Please answer separately for adolescents and adults. If not often or never, indicate reasons such as safety concerns, liability concerns, lack of training, appropriateness for the patient population, or practice protocols. You may also specify other reasons. 12. Quick Start for IUDs: In the past year, how often have you initiated IUDs (Cu-IUD or LNG-IUD) on the same day as the patient’s visit, regardless of menstrual timing, if reasonably certain the patient is not pregnant? Please answer separately for adolescents and adults. If not often or never, indicate reasons such as unavailability of IUDs, safety concerns, liability concerns, lack of training, appropriateness for the patient population, or practice protocols. You may also specify other reasons. 13. Quick Start for Implants: In the past year, how often have you initiated contraceptive implants on the same day as the patient’s visit, regardless of menstrual timing, if reasonably certain the patient is not pregnant? Please answer separately for adolescents and adults. If not often or never, indicate reasons such as unavailability of implants, safety concerns, liability concerns, lack of training, appropriateness for the patient population, or practice protocols. You may also specify other reasons. 14. Routine Pregnancy Testing: Do patients in your practice routinely undergo a urine pregnancy test before starting a contraceptive method? Please answer yes or no. 15. Timing of Contraceptive Initiation: Indicate when a woman can initiate the following contraceptive methods: oral contraceptives (all types), injectables (DMPA or NET-EN), implants, and IUDs. Options include any time if reasonably certain the woman is not pregnant, within seven days after the start of normal menses, or on the same day after an abortion. 16. Barriers to Providing Contraceptives: In the past month, how often have you been unable to provide a woman with her desired contraceptive method at the time of her visit? 17. Counseling Practices: In the past month, how often have you or your clinical team provided the following counseling services to female patients of reproductive age? These include: Instructions on correct use of their contraceptive method. Guidance on what to do if a dose is late or missed. Assistance in identifying and addressing potential barriers to correct use of their chosen method. Counseling on possible changes in menstrual bleeding. Information on return to fertility after discontinuing a method. Guidance on discontinuing or switching methods. Information on obtaining emergency contraception. Counseling on condom use for STD prevention.
